figures.caption: Fig. 1: Motivation and method comparison. (a) EEG visual decoding aims to align neural responses with visual semantics, but is challenged by subject variability and non-stationary data distributions. (b) Under realistic cross-subject generalization and continual adaptation settings, the baseline method [1] exhibits substantial performance degradation, whereas our method consistently improves decoding robustness, especially in continual adaptation. (c) The baseline loss landscape contains dense and sharp contours, reflecting unstable optimization and poor robustness to distribution shifts. (d) Our method produces a smoother and flatter loss landscape with lower loss values, indicating more stable and generalizable optimization. (e) Representative image reconstruction results, including successful cases ( ) and failure cases ( ).

Fig. 2: Overview of ProCA. ProCA learns EEG representations by progressively aligning them with frozen vision–language embeddings through confusion-guided contrastive supervision (see Sect. IV-B), while applying structure-consistent interpolation to preserve important channel-wise and temporal EEG components (see Sect. IV-C).

Fig. 5: Comparison with Euclidean Alignment (EA) on subjectindependent EEG visual decoding. (a) and (b) show that ProCA achieves the best average Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy across 200-, 150-, and 100-way retrieval settings. (c) and (d) further visualize subjectwise gains of ProCA over NeuroBridge and NeuroBridge with EA, respectively, indicating that ProCA provides consistent improvements beyond conventional alignment preprocessing.

Fig. 6: Loss landscape sharpness comparison across ten subjects and three EEG visual decoding baselines. The left column reports the maximum Hessian eigenvalue λmax, and the right column reports the Hessian trace. Lower values indicate flatter local minima. ProCA generally reduces both measures across baselines, indicating smoother optimization landscapes and improved representation robustness.

Fig. A11: Hyperparameter sensitivity analysis on the 150-way setting. Top: Top-1 accuracy; Bottom: Top-5 accuracy. Left: performance under different values of αmax with the transition epoch fixed to 25. Right: performance under different transition epochs with αmax = 0.8. Consistent with the 100-way setting, ProCA remains robust to hyperparameter variations and achieves its best performance at an intermediate transition stage across both evaluated accuracy metrics and parameter ranges.
